instruction: Pick up the key, hand it over to the other hand, insert it into the keyhole, then turn it.

arguments.note: The key lies on the right and the lock on the left. I turn the right wrist downward to approach the key.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 31 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: The wrist view shows the key to the left of the right hand. I move above its bow and finish the downward orientation.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 17 waypoints (0.7s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I descend above the round bow, leaving clearance for a final visual correction before closing.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 8 waypoints (0.3s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The bow is nearly centered between the jaws. I lower to just above the table grasp height.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 2 waypoints (0.1s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The close view shows the bow still beyond the finger centers toward the near table edge. I shift toward it with a little table clearance.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 4 waypoints (0.2s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The bow is now centered in the close wrist view. I descend carefully to the flat-key grasp height.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 2 waypoints (0.1s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I lower the final few millimetres and close on the key bow.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 7 waypoints (0.3s). The last 6 move the gripper, once the arm has arrived. The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The key is visibly captured between the closed jaws. I lift it clear of the table for the handover.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 10 waypoints (0.4s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I bring the lifted key into the shared workspace, keeping its bow accessible to the other hand from the near side.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 28 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: The key is securely lifted. I bring the open left hand toward the exposed bow from the near side for the transfer.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 34 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: The previous reach stopped early. I complete the approach, stopping short of the exposed bow.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 13 waypoints (0.5s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The left wrist sees the exposed bow centered ahead. I approach its edge before the final small closing motion.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 1 waypoints (0.0s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I advance four millimetres and close the left jaws around the exposed bow while the right hand still supports the key.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 7 waypoints (0.3s). The last 6 move the gripper, once the arm has arrived. The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The left jaws have closed on the bow. I release the right grip to complete the handover.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 6 waypoints (0.2s). The last 6 move the gripper, once the arm has arrived.

arguments.note: The key slipped during transfer and is visible on the table. I clear the right hand and reorient the left hand to recover the bow.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 52 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: I continue turning the left tool downward and open it for a recovery grasp.

calls.tool_result: left arm pose unreachable (planner status: Fail). The robot did not move; choose another pose. Neither arm moved.

arguments.note: The wrist turn was unreachable at the extended pose. I retract the left hand into a more comfortable workspace before turning.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 17 waypoints (0.7s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: With the hand retracted, I turn down toward the fallen key and reopen the jaws.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 39 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: I position the left hand over the recovered bow with the jaws across the key shaft.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 42 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: The motion stopped before the jaws opened. I finish aligning above the bow and open the gripper.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 21 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: The recovered bow is between the open jaws. I lower to just above table contact.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 2 waypoints (0.1s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I close the left jaws at the table-limited grasp height to recover the key.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 7 waypoints (0.3s). The last 6 move the gripper, once the arm has arrived. The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: The bow is captured in the left hand. I lift and carry it toward the lock with clearance for reorientation.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: playing 10 waypoints (0.4s). The next observation reports how close the grasp point landed.

arguments.note: I rotate the held key so its free shaft points down toward the top-facing keyhole.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 23 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.note: I adjust the wrist so the key shaft is vertical for the top-facing slot.

calls.tool_result: Accepted: the original plan contains 49 control steps; only its first 20 will execute before the next observation. The remaining steps will not execute automatically. This prefix may end before the target or before a scheduled gripper change; the next observation reports actual execution and target error.

arguments.hindsight: The initial pickup succeeded, but the handover missed the bow and dropped the key. Recovery succeeded with the left hand, while repeated truncated wrist rotations consumed the remaining budget. A closer verified handover grasp and smaller staged rotations would have preserved time for insertion.
arguments.reason: Insufficient motion budget remains to align, insert, turn the key, and return both arms home.
